newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE near agreement on Albania mission.
newsitem.headline: OSCE near agreement on Albania mission.

text.p: Europe's top security body OSCE was close to agreeing on Wednesday on the framework for a broad international military force to protect aid distribution in Albania, diplomatic sources said.

Ambassadors of the 54-member Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe had agreed in principle that the OSCE would lead an international effort in the crisis-torn Balkan state, but were seeking a green light from the United Nations, the sources said.

"The meeting is hoping to decide on an OSCE endorsement of a (U.N.) Security Council mandate, in other words it will encourage the Security Council to give its blessing (to the operation)," a diplomat told reporters.

Ambassadors were reconvening at 1500 GMT to continue discussions. Diplomats said they were looking at a multinational force "of the willing" that would probably include Italy, Spain, Greece, France and several others.
There was broad consensus that former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, the OSCE's peace envoy to Albania, should head the operation.
Diplomats said the only stumbling block to an agreement was an Albanian government request for more time to look at the draft decision.
"This is something that should be decided today. As soon as the elements are in place, we are ready to go immediately," one diplomat said.
The diplomats said it would be up to the countries involved to decide on the size of the force needed to enable civilian aid to reach its destination.
